title: Rabbi Nechunya the Great

paragraphs: [Megillah 28a](https://www.sefaria.org/Megillah.28a.10-12) relates that Rabbi Akiva asked him why he had lived so long. The attendants began beating Akiva, who climbed a palm tree and called out: “Master! If ‘lamb’ is stated, why add ‘one’?” Rabbi Nechunya told them: “He is a Torah scholar; leave him alone.” He answered: “‘One’ means the choicest of the flock.” He then said: “I never accepted gifts, never insisted on my rights, and was generous with my money.”[^2]
And from this it somewhat implies that Rabbi Nehunya the Great is not Rabbi Nehunya ben HaKaneh.[^1]

notes.text: Hyman cautiously infers that Nechunya the Great differs from Nechunya ben HaKaneh; the distinction remains tentative.

The linked exchange has Rabbi Akiva question Rabbi Nechunya the Great. [An earlier exchange on the same folio](https://www.sefaria.org/Megillah.28a.6) has disciples question Rabbi Nechunya ben HaKaneh. Both answers mention generosity with money. [Heilprin](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=2639&lang=en) refers the reader from the Great to ben HaKaneh. Hyman tentatively distinguishes the two.
